mbm-2251.clue: My best portrait took a whole roll and one tall pair of boots.
mbm-2251.quote: I lay in a puddle to catch our crossing guard reflected upside down. She held traffic to let me finish. On her mantel she keeps the print upside down too.

mbm-2252.clue: One passenger always gets the bow seat.
mbm-2252.quote: I put my niece’s stuffed moose in the front of my canoe while she was away at camp. I paddled him round the lake and mailed her the captain’s portrait.

mbm-2253.clue: The blue tile tells me when I can turn around.
mbm-2253.quote: My first time swimming a whole length without stopping, my little brother followed me along the pool deck in his socks. When I came up at the blue tile he was wetter than I was.

mbm-2254.clue: We all wanted to buy the crooked house.
mbm-2254.quote: I built a cardboard town for game night. One house came out leaning so we made rent cheaper there. Now everybody fights over it and the rest of my street sits empty.

mbm-2255.quote: At the outdoor spring I watch a dragonfly patrol the same three stones. When it lands I count that as the end of a lap. I have no idea how long I stayed.

mbm-2256.clue: You can hear the difference with your eyes shut.
mbm-2256.quote: My dad’s baduk stones make a little clink in their bowls. Mine are buttons from an old coat. We mixed the sets one night and now his fancy board wears a sleeve.

mbm-2257.clue: The drum case still has a dress pocket.
mbm-2257.quote: My sister outgrew her red corduroy dress. I stitched it into a case for her snare, pocket and all. She keeps her lucky drum key right where she used to stash gum.

mbm-2258.clue: The quietest rep is the important one.
mbm-2258.quote: My downstairs neighbor works nights. I built a rubber cradle for my dumbbells and learned to set them down gently. She sent up banana bread after her first full Saturday of sleep.

mbm-2259.clue: I leave the orange ball in the hedge.
mbm-2259.quote: I found my first golf ball under a bush at the public course. Last week a kid in a borrowed cap was looking for one. I put an orange ball where mine had been.

mbm-2260.clue: I can fit the whole landing field in one pocket.
mbm-2260.quote: After my first jump I sewed a green felt map onto my gear bag. That tiny yellow square is where I meant to land. The sheep I added later tells you where I actually did.

mbm-2261.clue: Listen for the one that rattles.
mbm-2261.quote: Two of my juggling balls are stuffed with rice. The third has one dry pea in a pill bottle inside. My granddad can call the good catches from his chair without looking up.

mbm-2262.clue: The silver spoon gets passed around.
mbm-2262.quote: The fair’s pudding contest gave me a fancy spoon. I brought it to Sunday lunch. My cousins kept sliding it down the table until the baby took first prize in mashed peas.

mbm-2263.clue: There’s a little crescent missing from my practice mat.
mbm-2263.quote: I rolled up my old judo mat for the last time and found the piece the puppy chewed off years ago. I trimmed that scrap into a key ring. Still bow when I open the gym.

mbm-2264.clue: You have to read this one in the right light.
mbm-2264.quote: My aunt wrote her pie recipe in pencil on the blank page of a mystery. Every time the detective finds the footprints I get hungry for lemon pie. I’ve baked it twice.

mbm-2265.clue: We needed a bigger curtain for the sequel.
mbm-2265.quote: I hung a white bedsheet between two apple trees for movie night. A moth crossed the projector beam and cast an enormous shadow. My neighbors still ask if the monster is coming back.

mbm-2266.clue: My champion has one corner missing.
mbm-2266.quote: A bus door clipped the corner off my favorite card’s sleeve. I drew a tiny bandage on the replacement. All my friends know that battered wizard on sight now.

mbm-2267.quote: I taught my home computer to draw a duck every time I typed the wrong command. My little sister added sunglasses. Now she sits there making perfectly deliberate mistakes.

mbm-2268.clue: I always bring a second pair of laces.
mbm-2268.quote: Our dance club has a black light over the floor. I thread one shoe with a neon lace so my friends can follow the footwork. Last month the whole front row turned green.

mbm-2269.clue: I can show you the short way home on my sleeve.
mbm-2269.quote: I stitched our weekend trail into my jacket cuff after my paper map got soaked. The blue stitch marks a creek. The big knot is where we sat and ate both lunches.

mbm-2270.clue: I keep score with my laundry.
mbm-2270.quote: We play dominoes till there’s no daylight on my steps. I clip a clothespin to the winner’s collar each round. You should see my uncle walk home on a good night.

mbm-2271.quote: The park set lost a knight, so I carved one from a peanut shell. A pigeon swooped in and captured it. Now I bring a spare knight and a very plain wooden box.

mbm-2272.clue: I’ve slept under a hundred little moons.
mbm-2272.quote: I saved foil sweet wrappers till I had enough to sew a moon inside my tent. When the wind moves the canvas my little moon breaks up into stars.

mbm-2273.clue: I take one lap with both hands empty.
mbm-2273.quote: I deliver the morning paper on my warmup run. At the last house an old man holds out an empty fist. We bump knuckles, and that’s the first mile officially done.

mbm-2274.clue: The last cut stays folded till the party.
mbm-2274.quote: I cut my brother’s old bicycle across a whole string of paper flags, even the bent back wheel. We unfolded it over his birthday table and he recognized his bike before he saw the cake.

mbm-2275.clue: I’m quicker with the napkins than I used to be.
mbm-2275.quote: My coat wore more syrup than my waffles did. At the end the judge hung the silver medal right over the biggest spot. That’s how I managed to look respectable in the photograph.
